config.title: useWindowSize

intro.title: useWindowSize
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a custom React hook called `useWindowSize` that tracks and returns the current width and height of the browser window. You will learn how to use the `useState` and `useEffect` hooks to manage state and handle side effects, such as listening to the `resize` event. The main technologies involved are React hooks and the browser's `window` object. By the end, you'll have a reusable hook that updates dynamically when the window size changes, enhancing your understanding of custom hooks and event handling in React.
intro.usecase: The useWindowSize hook is essential for creating responsive layouts that adapt to the user's viewport. Developers use it in dashboards to rearrange charts and tables on different screen sizes, in e-commerce sites to adjust product grids, and in navigation menus to switch between desktop and mobile versions. This pattern ensures UI components like modals, side panels, and image galleries resize appropriately, providing a consistent experience across devices. Implementing it helps avoid layout breaks and improves usability in real-world applications like analytics tools, admin panels, and media-rich websites.

objectives: Implement a custom React hook that tracks browser window dimensions
Initialize state variables to store current width and height values
Construct an event listener to detect window resize events
Manipulate state values when the window size changes
Apply cleanup logic to remove event listeners when the component unmounts
Integrate the useWindowSize hook into functional components
Render responsive UI elements based on dynamic window dimensions
